[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Django: Models, Views, Templates, and Admin Interface"},{"order":2,"type":"subheading","text":"Introduction"},{"order":3,"type":"paragraph","text":"Django is a high-level Python web framework that encourages rapid development and clean, pragmatic design. It follows the Model-View-Template (MVT) architectural pattern. This tutorial will guide you through the core components: Models, Views, Templates, and the Admin interface."},{"order":4,"type":"subheading","text":"Models"},{"order":5,"type":"paragraph","text":"Models are Python classes that represent database tables. Each attribute of the model represents a database field. Django provides an ORM (Object-Relational Mapper) that allows you to interact with the database using Python code instead of raw SQL."},{"order":6,"type":"code","text":"# models.py from django.db import models class Product(models.Model): name = models.CharField(max_length=200) description = models.TextField() price = models.DecimalField(max_digits=10, decimal_places=2) created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True) def __str__(self): return self.name"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Explanation: - 'name' is a CharField, storing strings up to 200 characters. - 'description' is a TextField, storing longer text. - 'price' is a DecimalField, storing decimal numbers with a maximum of 10 digits and 2 decimal places. - 'created_at' is a DateTimeField, automatically set to the current time when the object is created. - '__str__' method returns a human-readable string representation of the object."},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"After defining your models, you need to create migrations and apply them to the database:"},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"python manage.py makemigrations python manage.py migrate"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Views"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Views are Python functions that receive a web request and return a web response. They handle the logic for processing requests and rendering templates."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"# views.py from django.shortcuts import render from .models import Product def product_list(request): products = Product.objects.all() return render(request, 'products/product_list.html', {'products': products})"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Explanation: - 'product_list' view retrieves all products from the database. - 'render' function renders the 'products/product_list.html' template, passing the 'products' data to it."},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"You need to map URLs to your views in 'urls.py':"},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"# urls.py from django.urls import path from . import views urlpatterns = [ path('products/', views.product_list, name='product_list'), ]"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Templates"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Templates are HTML files that define the structure and presentation of your web pages. Django's template engine allows you to embed dynamic content into your templates using template tags and variables."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"{% load static %} Product List

Product List

    {% for product in products %}
  • {{ product.name }} - ${{ product.price }}
    • {% endfor %}
"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"Explanation: - '{% for product in products %}' iterates through the 'products' list passed from the view. - '{{ product.name }}' and '{{ product.price }}' display the name and price of each product."},{"order":20,"type":"subheading","text":"Admin Interface"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"Django provides a powerful admin interface that allows you to easily manage your data. To enable the admin interface, you need to create a superuser and register your models in 'admin.py'."},{"order":22,"type":"code","text":"python manage.py createsuperuser"},{"order":23,"type":"code","text":"# admin.py from django.contrib import admin from .models import Product admin.site.register(Product)"},{"order":24,"type":"paragraph","text":"Now, you can access the admin interface by navigating to '/admin/' in your browser and logging in with the superuser credentials."},{"order":25,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":26,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial covered the basics of Django's Models, Views, Templates, and Admin interface. These are the fundamental building blocks for creating web applications with Django. Further exploration of Django's features and documentation will enable you to build more complex and sophisticated applications."}]
